title: Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding
technique: speculative decoding: small approximation model drafts gamma tokens, target verifies in parallel with rejection sampling preserving output distribution

optimized_metrics.evidence: Specifically, we are able to accelerate inference without changing the model architectures, without changing the training-procedures or needing to re-train the models, and without changing the model output distribution.
without changing the model output distribution

headline_claim.text: we get meaningful 2X-3X speedups in practice vs T5X, a popular optimized implementation.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 4, Table 1 (increase in total arithmetic operations)

tradeoff_acknowledged: latency is improved through increased concurrency at the cost of an increased number of arithmetic operations (e.g. Table 1); not helpful when additional compute is unavailable
models: T5-XXL (11B) target with T5-small/base/large drafters; GPT-like 97M, LaMDA 137B alpha measurements
workloads: WMT EnDe translation, CNN/DM summarization (T5X baseline)
extractor_notes: Analytical + small empirical. Paper uses 'latency' / 'walltime' for the speed metric; no serving throughput. The headline is per-request decoding speedup (improvement factor), batch 1. alpha measured also for LaMDA and GPT-like models without end-to-end implementation.
